test/lolcat/{core,lib}.clj ported (EPL 2.0). ThreadLocal -> atom (lolcat drives callbacks synchronously by design; a dynamic var cannot propagate a child fiber's mutation back). fn-name now reads a :lolcat/name the defword macro attaches, because jolt's printed fn name carries no user name. lolcat's own -rotn-test and bi-test pass.

ebb.impl.util hardened; ADR-001 discipline #1 rewritten from the Java sources (CAS-on-one-atom vs locking, split per impl, callbacks outside the critical section); ebb.impl.event ports Event for cancellation identity under CAS retry.

dfv/rdv/sem/mbx ported as CAS-on-one-atom per ADR-001, with Event for cancellation identity. Missionary's dfv_test, rdv_test, sem_test and mbx_test pass unchanged apart from (partial instance? Cancelled) -> m/cancelled?. sem_test/holding deferred to ebb-8nq.14. Also added ebb.concurrency-test, which reproduced the spike's fiber deadlock as a timed failure before the fix.

ebb.impl.race-join ports RaceJoin.cljs logic with RaceJoin.java's two atomic counters (race -2/-1/index, join count), including the -2 -> -1 CAS that makes a synchronously-completing child safe. core/join and core/race now go through it. missionary's join_test and race_test pass unchanged.

Seed, Reduce, Never, Sleep in place; missionary's seed_test, reduce_test and never_test pass. seed_test needed one hand edit (#(instance? Cancelled %) -> m/cancelled?) that the port script flagged. Missionary has no sleep_test; ebb.smoke-test covers sleep including cancellation.

sp is a fiber with the readiness handshake (ebb.impl.affine), so missionary's start ordering holds. Closed ahead of ebb-8nq.13 because the part of .13 sp needed (the owner fiber) is done; what remains there is the call/cc pair for ap/cp, which sp does not use. Cancellation-token semantics split out as ebb-8nq.19.

Cancellation token ported from Sequential.java into ebb.impl.affine as a CAS-driven atom (missionary holds it under the process monitor; ebb's body runs on its own fiber). kill nulls-and-invokes, arm! cancels a task registered after death, check/m/! throws once dead. Cancelling cancels the parked task and surfaces Cancelled at the ? -- it does not stop the body, matching missionary and Erlang.

Also needed and delivered: the RESUME handshake. sp_test failed without it, because missionary's success callback drives the body to its next park before returning and lolcat depends on that. resume! now installs a gate, delivers, and waits for quiescence -- the same gen_server:call shape as the start handshake, generalised.

7 new spec tests in ebb.sp-cancel-test (missionary's suite covers only success/failure). Mutation-checked: no-op kill fails 5 of them, and dropping arm!'s dead-token branch fails exactly the test written for it. Suite 50 tests / 86 assertions green; sp_test and compel_test now pass unchanged.

ebb.impl.prompt: delimited, multi-shot continuations for ap/cp, plus both guards.

Research: Chez 10.4.1 has NO native prompts (verified -- no call-with-prompt/abort-to-prompt/shift/prompt tags). Rejected the Dybvig/Peyton Jones/Sabry delimcc library on Oleg Kiselyov's caveat that it 'must be used with extreme care in the presence of other effects: dynamic binding, exceptions, or independent uses of call/cc' -- ebb has all three, jolt's fiber park being itself a call/1cc capture. Built the narrow prompt instead, in the Guile Fibers shape: the driver re-enters the continuation, the continuation never calls the driver.

Two non-obvious mechanics, both found the hard way and commented in the file:
 * the normal return must go through the prompt cell, RE-READ at return time -- otherwise every resume delivers its value to the first driver call and splices the driver's continuation into k (observed as the driver running twice per fork).
 * that read must happen AFTER the thunk runs; (@cell [::value (thunk)]) evaluates the operator first and captures the stale delimiter.
 * a dynamic binding cannot hold the cell: bindings survive a capture but NOT a re-entry.

Guards, each mutation-checked to fail without its test: same-fiber resume (a cross-fiber resume is a documented hang, so it throws) and no-fork-inside-finally (measured N+1 finally runs for N branches; catch is unaffected, fiber parks are unaffected, and a finally outside the prompt does not count).

7 tests / 16 assertions in ebb.prompt-test; suite 57 tests / 102 assertions green. ap (ebb-8nq.15) can now be built on start/resume/suspend.

ap, ?>, amb, amb= on multi-shot delimited continuations. missionary's ap_test (all 7: ?, ?-cancel-with-failure, ?>, ?>-cancel-with-crash, ?>-parallel, amb, amb=) and none_test pass unchanged, plus 8 end-to-end semantics tests in ebb.ap-semantics-test.

Substrate swap: where missionary's backtrack calls cloroutine's clone arity ((.-coroutine p) boot c), ebb resumes the same prompt continuation again -- resuming k twice IS the clone. No fiber is involved in an ap body; the prompt handles every suspension.

Four things found while building, all now commented in the code:
 * PROMPT BUG: an exception thrown inside a RESUMED extent unwinds along the reinstated stack and lands in whatever try/catch sat below the ORIGINAL start, which then carries on as if the first entry had returned -- the driver ran twice. start now routes throws through the cell as [::error e], the catch being part of the extent so it is reinstated with each resume.
 * GUARD FALSE POSITIVE: the finally-depth base must be recorded at start and never again. Re-recording on resume compares the extent's winder chain against the RESUMER's; a timer-thread resume of a prompt started inside clojure.test's try/finally read as 'fork inside 4 finallys'.
 * NESTED FORKS need the parent link missionary keeps in its Branch/Choice tree. A branch leaves its choice either by producing a value (slot freed on transfer) or by FORKING, and then the slot is held until the child subtree is exhausted. Without reap!, a nested ?> wedges the outer fork forever. This is the one place the flat model had to grow a tree.
 * An eager flow (seed) notifies from inside (flow n t), before the iterator is assigned; the armed flag closes that window.

Also fixed ebb.impl.seed for an empty collection ((seq []) is nil, so .iterator blew up).

Suite 73 tests / 121 assertions green.

Both halves done.

1. Affinity identity is now (thread, fiber), not fiber alone. current-fiber is nil off a fiber, so the old check passed vacuously between two OS threads. New prompt test spawns a plain Thread and asserts the resume is refused; reverting to fiber-only fails it.

2. ap now marshals. Tightening the guard turned the previously-silent violation into a hang, which is the honest failure -- ebb.ap-semantics-test/a-branch-can-park was resuming a main-thread continuation from the timer thread. Fixed properly per ADR-001: the ap process is an Erlang-shaped server with one owner fiber and an inbox, and every entry point (upstream notify/terminate, task completion, downstream transfer, cancel) is a gen_server:call through it. A call already on the owner runs inline, which is the common path. The inbox closes when the process terminates so the owner fiber does not leak.

Mutation-checked both ways: fiber-only identity fails the new prompt test; making call! always inline hangs the ap semantics suite.

Suite 74 tests / 122 assertions green. ADR-001 updated -- discipline 2 now covers the server shape, and it is the same conclusion sp reached from the other direction.

cp and ?< on the prompt. missionary's cp_test passes unchanged (all 9: pure-success, pure-failure, ident-success, ident-failure, ident-duplicate, lazy-switch, input-change-from-continuation, undefined-input, switch-both-ready), plus 6 end-to-end tests in ebb.cp-semantics-test and a watch impl to drive them.

cp is an incremental computation, and the prompt fits it directly: each ?< is a memo point, and a change re-resumes THAT continuation with the new value while pruning the choices the invalidated continuation had created. Ranks in creation order stand in for missionary's pairing heap -- lowest dirty rank wins.

Four semantics that had to be matched exactly, each now commented:
 * downstream must NOT be notified while a sample is in flight; an upstream notifying mid-transfer is supplying the value being read, not invalidating it (missionary's (identical? ps (.-value ps)) guard).
 * a DUPLICATE value does not invalidate: re-emitting the same value leaves the continuation valid and is not recomputed (missionary compares in ).
 * an unready flow is not a continuous flow -- cancel it, let the cancellation's notify be drained, then report 'Undefined continuous flow.'
 * transfer LOOPS. The body can make an upstream notify (input-change-from-continuation), and a pruned choice whose upstream had already notified still owes a transfer, drained after the live work as missionary does.

Mutation-checked: removing duplicate suppression, the prune, or the sampling guard each breaks the suite.

Suite 89 tests / 144 assertions green.

Zip, Latest (with PairingHeap) and Sample ported. missionary's zip_test (5), latest_test (8) and sample_test (5) pass unchanged. Sync strategy taken from each Java file per ADR-001: Zip needs none (its pending counter serialises), Latest is CAS-shaped, Sample's regions are already serialised by the busy/done toggle.

Relieve, Buffer, Eduction and Reductions ported; missionary's relieve_test, buffer_test, eduction_test and reductions_test all pass unchanged (20 tests). Added bin/port-impl to mechanise the cljs-to-jolt translation. One real host difference: Eduction keeps a growable JS array and calls .push, which a jolt array cannot do, so the buffer now doubles -- caught by the cat-transducer case, where the transducer emits more values than it consumes.

GroupBy, Watch, Observe and Store ported; missionary's group_by_test (7), watch_test, observe_test and store_test all pass unchanged (18 tests). Host differences fixed: cljs ->MapEntry becomes clojure.lang.MapEntry., js/Error becomes ex-info, and the ns name must use hyphens even though the file uses underscores (jolt read ebb.impl.group_by as a class token otherwise). bin/port-impl now handles all three.

Propagator (563 lines) and Reactor ported; signal, stream, memo, reactor, signal! and stream! wired into ebb.core. missionary's propagator_test passes (18 tests; they assert via lolcat.lib/run rather than clojure.test/is, so the runner counts 0 assertions -- mutation-checked: disabling publisher gives 18 errors, disabling signal gives 10).

One real host difference: the cljs impls keep mutable top-level state as plain def plus set!, which ClojureScript allows and jolt does not -- set! on a var needs a thread-local binding. Propagator's rank counter and Reactor's current/delayed globals are atoms now.

ebb.core public API filled in: 50 vars covering tasks (sleep, join, race, any, timeout, compel, never, absolve, attempt, memo), ports (dfv, mbx, rdv, sem, store, holding), flows (seed, reduce, reductions, eduction, relieve, buffer, zip, latest, sample, group-by, watch, observe, signal, stream, reactor, none), and the three process primitives with their operators (sp/ap/cp, ?, ?>, ?<, !, amb, amb=). via/blk/cpu and publisher/subscribe are deliberately absent per doc/conformance.md.

Also ported missionary's tck harness as ebb.tck (task-spec/flow-spec/deftask/defflow verbatim; check! rewritten off LinkedBlockingQueue/ArrayDeque/AtomicReference/timer-threads onto a vector, a channel and the runtime deadline heap) and its core_test as ebb.core-test -- 56 broad integration tests, of which 17 currently fail. Filed as ebb-8nq.21.

doc/conformance.md written: deliberately absent APIs, behavioural differences (Cancelled as a value, ? at any call depth, the fork-in-finally refusal, executor affinity, the ap/cp scheduling hop), host differences inherited from jolt (codepoint strings, value-comparing compare-and-set!, no thread interruption), the tck driver rewrite and why it was needed, the one known flaky test with its measurement, tests not ported, and implementation notes that are not divergences.

Not done, and worth its own bead if wanted: the automated GATE the original description asked for -- jolt fails 'make certify' on a new unlisted divergence. Ebb has the registry but nothing enforces it.

All 17 fixed. Five root causes, each recorded in the notes above: (1) resume! coupled one process's unwinding to another's progress -- handshake now scoped to the boundary; (2) reactor had two porting slips, an unqualified reify protocol and three bare global reads my regex skipped; (3) ?< inside ap was never implemented, it is a fork with parallelism -1; (4) the tck driver needed timeouts to be lowest-priority; (5) the prompt cell went stale because an extent returns through whichever delimiter the cell holds, abandoning the entering frame -- now keyed by executor, ADR-001 rule 4.

225/225 on a clean run. What remains is smaller and split out as ebb-8nq.23: about one run in four fails exactly one timing-sensitive test in core_test.
